problem: The chapter says a preference value is only a String, int, boolean, long or float, and tells students lists belong to file storage or SQLite. SharedPreferences also has putStringSet/getStringSet for a Set of Strings, so a student who answers 'lists are impossible' in an exam is technically wrong.
fix: Add: 'A value can also be a Set of Strings, written with putStringSet and read with getStringSet. That is the only collection type allowed, and it suits a handful of short strings (say, favourite team names), not a thousand scores.' Then in Q2 the answer list becomes String, int, boolean, long, float and Set of Strings.

problem: The chapter tells students to register an OnSharedPreferenceChangeListener but not that SharedPreferences holds listeners weakly. A listener created as a temporary object with nothing else pointing at it can be garbage collected and silently stop firing, which is a common bug for students doing Q7 exactly as written.
fix: Add: 'Keep the listener in a field of the Activity or Fragment. SharedPreferences holds registered listeners weakly, so a listener with no other reference can be collected and stop firing.'

problem: The chapter points students to EncryptedSharedPreferences as the current way to store secrets, but the Jetpack security-crypto library that provides it has since been deprecated, so the pointer is out of date.
fix: Say instead: 'EncryptedSharedPreferences wrapped the same key-value idea with keys held by the Android Keystore, but that library is now deprecated; for secrets, check the current Android guidance on the Keystore or on a server-side token store.'
